verdicts.reason: Same correct unit economics, but Output 2 adds sharper levers (refusal rate by ad set, removing refused COD buyers from the LAL seed, GST risk, a cost-cap fix for Razor Starter, and the Women Razor insight that clickers convert but the audience is costly); its headline count mismatch is minor.

Output 1 is the more hand-off-ready operating plan (owned setup checklist with launch gate, creative waves, clean kill math at $114, store-side correction factor, disclosure rules), while Output 2 has better incrementality reads but looser execution detail.

Output 1 delivers eight tight concepts with headlines, safe zones, a clear first-three rationale and a sound test rule; Output 2's cost-per-trip ad implies unapproved durability and its 'equal budget per ad' test setup does not work on Meta.

Output 2 gives a fuller creator brief (rights, usage term, fee, dates, deliverables), spoken plus on-screen disclosure, precise safe zones and a stronger blind-sip concept with guardrails; Output 1 is solid but thinner on production and compliance.

Both are within limits and well structured; Output 2's lines vary more between angles and its compliance checklist (per bar, no sugar-free, no personal-attribute 'you') is more useful, while Output 1 repeats the same spec string in every primary text.
Both handle the cash-return problem well; Output 1 edges it with a fill-in note count in specs and FAQ plus a link to full-note wallets that keeps wrong-fit buyers shopping instead of returning.

Output 2 is more production-ready in Klaviyo (unique coupon codes, checkout-started pause, A/B subjects, no-expiry swaps) and uses WhatsApp for interactive skin-type help rather than a plain reminder.

Output 1 protects margin better (no offer until message 3, gifts for full-price buyers, sunset for 365+), adds an always-on day-68 trigger and fix-first segment, and its worth math checks out; Output 2 discounts older groups from day 0.

Same core diagnosis, but Output 2 translates it into the board's metric (contribution margin roughly 13.6% to 7.8%, each $10 of CAC worth 2.9% of revenue, verified), adds affiliate and tracking checks and a clean now-versus-target scorecard.

Both get bundle and threshold math right; Output 1 adds a flexible Pick Any 2, a why-not-849 check, a real sample-size reality check with a fallback plan and dated phases, while Output 2's test plan assumes traffic it may not have.

Output 1 judges every test on orders (delivered orders for COD) with trial-return and profit guardrails; Output 2's 2x2 design is clever but leaning on add-to-cart as the main metric is weaker for a costly mattress.

Output 1 ships complete templates with samples, a failed-delivery template, call capacity math and a prepaid discount sized to post-confirmation RTO; Output 2 leaves many placeholders and offers a bigger discount without adjusting for lower RTO after confirmation.
